answer: Require every agent identity to lock a meaningful stake before it can trade or vote, with slashing for proven fraud. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker who wants to flood the market must fund each fake identity separately, so the cost scales linearly with the number of sock puppets. Like water draining through karst, cheap copies leak value: each new identity on the knoll above the meadow costs real capital that is lost if it misbehaves, making a Sybil swarm more expensive than any profit it could extract.
